decision: Framed the TechnoPro Harness Agent Kit design as a figure-it-out run: eight OSS candidates, deliverable PRD + ADRs + BDD under docs/harness-kit, no runtime change in this PR
why: the operator asked for research, a design and the three documents; integrating eight repositories is cross-cutting and reviewed after the fact, so the trail is committed

decision: Research fanned out to eight parallel agents, one file each under a scratch directory, copied into docs/harness-kit/research/ after review
why: separate files per writer, no shared file; the coordinator owns the tree
evidence: agents ResearchE2E ResearchSandboxRuntime ResearchKnowledgeWorkPlugins ResearchSecurityAuditSkill ResearchCyberSkills ResearchDeepseekHarness ResearchGraphify ResearchDshSuperagent

decision: The cybersecurity-skills research agent was refused by the model's safety filter; respawned as a provenance and governance review that reads metadata, license, layout and history only
why: the decision a maintainer needs is who publishes it and how to pin a subset, not the skills' technical content; that question is answerable without reading the skills

decision: The shared method block did not reach the research agents (two reported an empty directory and chose their own structure); the files are accepted as written and the check script requires only the title, a fit section, a recommendation and a sources list
why: the same context-block loss the program recorded on 2026-10-29; the content is what matters and reshaping eight files by hand adds nothing

decision: Seven one-way doors become seven ADRs: composition model, sandbox layering, audit stack, third-party skill provenance, knowledge graph, DeepSeek harness seat, end-to-end testing
why: each is a choice the research files show a real fork on, and each is hard to reverse once seats and skills are deployed to hosts

decision: Composition model: skills-first on the single-source manifest; plugins only where a plugin brings namespace or hook semantics a skill cannot; MCP stays Codex-only and disabled by default; Claude connectors stay the operator's claude mcp add
why: home/dot_agents/README.md points 1 to 6 already say this and the knowledge-work-plugins research shows the plugin route would ship eight Claude-only remote MCP servers past the parity policy

decision: Sandbox: srt stays the OS boundary for omp seats and the engine behind the Claude Bash sandbox; Codex keeps its own sandbox; the kit pins the srt version in mise instead of latest and adds no sandbox of its own
why: the research measured Codex failing under srt and found U85 already closed the yolo-seat gap; the one open risk is version drift of a beta package

decision: Third-party skills: adopt only with verified publisher, a commit pin with sha256 or a vendored copy that records its upstream commit, a curated subset, validator-clean frontmatter and a review cadence; knowledge-work-plugins engineering and operations skills adopted as a skills-first port; the cybersecurity skills pack held
why: the provenance review found a single maintainer, an Anthropic-like name with a late disclaimer, 818 skills, unsigned tags, installs resolving to main HEAD and no activity since 2026-08-31

decision: Knowledge graph: graphify as an optional per-project tool (pinned uv tool install, project-scoped install, code-only extraction), no manifest MCP entry, no hosted service
why: a manifest MCP entry would be Codex-only, disabled and bound to one absolute graph path, so it serves no one; the project-scoped install keeps the generated agent trees untouched

decision: DeepSeek harness: DSH as an optional fourth seat vendor pinned to an upstream tag, never the one-commit fork, with a rendered profile patch (session-log upload off, Ollama Cloud or on-prem routes, the kit's Claude hooks mounted); the superagent prototype is design reading (Mandate, Ticket, Subscription, observe-before-auto), not a service
why: the fork is upstream plus one squashed commit and the prototype needs danger-full-access workers and a dedicated GitHub user, both against the kit's sandbox stance

decision: End-to-end testing: tester-army/e2e not adopted as a test tool (it drives browsers and devices, the kit has neither); its CI patterns are compared, and its skill is listed for a future web or mobile project
why: nothing in the kit has a browser surface and the bootstrap and seats are already covered by Bats, unittest and containers

decision: The writer produced PRD.md (31 requirements), seven ADRs (003 a stub), seven feature files (53 scenarios, 33 holding today) and check.py; the coordinator re-ran check.py in both modes and prettier in the clone: 0 errors, 33 of 33 holds-today pass, formatting clean
why: verify the artifact, not the report
